newsitem.title: MEXICO: ICA Q3 construction operating margin rose.
newsitem.headline: ICA Q3 construction operating margin rose.

text.p: Mexico's Empresas ICA raised the operating margin in its key construction division in the third quarter to 10.8 percent from 4.4 percent in the second quarter, company figures released Monday showed.

ICA said that its construction division -- made up of heavy, industrial and urban/housing sections -- earned revenues of 1.36 billion pesos in the third quarter compared to 1.38 billion in the second quarter (in end-September pesos) and showed an operating profit of 148 million pesos compared to 58 million.
The heavy construction section had third quarter revenues of 672 million pesos, which ICA said was a 36 percent increase over the same year-ago period.

ICA said that result was mostly due to its Spanish unit Rodio Cimentaciones Especiales, which made up 39 percent of the section's revenues in the third quarter of 1996 and were not included in the year-ago period's results.

"The operating profit of the heavy construction section shows a result of 37 million pesos and an operating margin of 5.6 percent in the third quarter," ICA said. In the second quarter the operating margin was two percent.
The heavy construction sector's operating profit in the third quarter was 121 million pesos lower than in the third quarter of last year, ICA said.

The company said its operating profit dropped due to spending on ongoing projects, including the final stages of construction of the Acapulco tunnel and improvements to the Texcoco-Ecatepec and Coatzacoalcos-Salina Cruz highways.

In industrial construction, ICA said revenues rose 67 percent year-on-year to 445 million pesos, with an operating profit of 97 million and an operating margin of 22 percent, well above the two percent registered in the year-ago period and the 7.5 percent seen in the second quarter of this year.
"The improvement in margins came from work done for (telecommunications venture) Avantel, Eastman and a dehydrosulphurisation plant for (state oil firm) Pemex", ICA said.
In its urban construction and housing section, ICA said third quarter revenues were 243 million pesos, down 1.6 percent from the same year-ago period.
Operating profit fell 61 percent to 14 million pesos, giving an operating margin of 5.7 percent. The fall was due to "greater competition in public tenders," ICA said.
ICA's revenues in other areas not related to construction rose 12.1 percent from a year ago to 399 million pesos in the third quarer.
